title: Why Are OU's Colors Crimson and Cream? The 1895 Origin Story
question: When did the University of Oklahoma choose crimson and cream as its colors?
answer: OU's colors were chosen in the fall of 1895 by a committee chaired by student May Overstreet, which picked crimson and cream. The colors have shifted toward crimson and white over time, but fans still call them crimson and cream.
summary: OU picked crimson and cream in fall 1895, when a committee led by May Overstreet chose the colors. Here is why fans still say cream though the look is white.
body: Ask any Oklahoma fan for the school colors and you will hear crimson and cream almost before you finish the question. That answer goes back to the fall of 1895, just a few years after the university was founded in 1890, when May Overstreet was asked to chair a committee to choose OU's colors.

The committee settled on crimson and cream, and the choice was revealed with an elaborate display of the colors draped above a platform in front of the student body. Students loved it. Pennants, banners and badges in the new colors quickly showed up in shop windows, classrooms and around town, and local merchants could not keep up with demand.

Here is the fun trivia twist. Over the decades the look on uniforms and merchandise has drifted from cream toward a crisper white, so what you see on the field today is mostly crimson and white. The OU Chant even sings of colors gleaming red and white. Even so, the original name stuck, and Sooners still proudly say crimson and cream.

The colors are a big part of game-day identity in Norman. Fans are urged to wear the official colors to home events, turning the stands into what the athletics department calls a sea of crimson. More than a century after Overstreet's committee made its pick, those colors remain one of the most recognizable looks in college football.
